model_interpretation.claim: Packing short H rows into each CTA should reduce CTA overhead and inactive threads in the separate forward and input-gradient passes. The mapping uses row_width=min(L,256) and packs floor(256/row_width) rows per CTA; for L=48, this assigns five rows to a 240-thread CTA instead of launching one 256-thread CTA per row. Rows of length at least 256 retain the existing one-row, 256-thread mapping. The baseline is correct at 35.464 ms mean for the full call, but it does not isolate these kernels; any benefit remains unmeasured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Map each forward and input-gradient CTA across multiple H rows when L is below 256: block.x is L and block.y is floor(256/L), with a bounds guard for incomplete H groups.","Keep 256-wide x tiles and one row per CTA for L >= 256, preserving the existing per-row output mapping for longer rows.","Retain the separate FP32 forward and input-gradient passes, their bounds-safe zero padding and complete writes; leave the weight-gradient kernel unchanged."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Grouping four neighboring j outputs in each CTA may amortize repeated gy loads while retaining a direct FP32 reduction over B and L for each output. The extra accumulators and four shared-memory reductions per CTA could offset that reuse. Earlier valid results show the one-stage CTA parent at 0.014375 s and the split-scratch variant at 0.019781 s mean complete-call time; this contrasting experiment avoids another scratch stage and must be judged on complete-call timing and correctness.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Changed the weight-gradient kernel to assign each CTA four neighboring j outputs for one h.","Each CTA traverses B and L using the existing thread layout, reuses one gy load across the four output accumulators, and performs four independent shared-memory FP32 reductions.","Preserved bounds checks and writes every valid gk output; the variant does not use scratch or allocate additional memory."]}

items.subject: Intégrer le mapping T1 au kernel gk b957
items.objective: Partir de b957, qui regroupe quatre sorties gk par CTA, et y intégrer uniquement le mapping séparé forward/input-gradient de f014. Ces changements visent des kernels distincts; mesurer la combinaison complète sans présumer d’un gain additif.
